# derived from monero v0.18.5.1 source, not captured from a run
# fields: COMMAND_RPC_STORE::response_t, src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server_commands_defs.h:990-994 --
#         EMPTY, and the request (:983-987) is empty too. The JSON-RPC result is {}.
# ITS ONLY CALLER IS send::relay, AFTER THE LAST SUCCESSFUL relay_tx (DESIGN.md §2a.4, §5b).
#         monero-wallet-rpc writes the wallet file only on a graceful stop()
#         (src/wallet/wallet_rpc_server.cpp:294-302, which calls m_wallet->store()), on THIS explicit
#         call (:2060-2077), or on the open/create paths' autosave_current. Its auto-refresh idle
#         handler NEVER stores (:210-285 -- it refreshes and nothing else).
#         So without this one extra RPC a SIGKILL, an OOM kill or a power cut after a relay loses the
#         wallet's own record of the outgoing transfer and its tx key. Funds are not lost -- a rescan
#         re-derives the spend -- but the §2a.4 resolve step then answers "not found" for a
#         transaction that really was broadcast, leaves the pending record in place, and blocks every
#         later send until the user runs clear-pending by hand: the habit §2a.4 exists to prevent.
# NOT IN DESIGN.md §8's deliverable list; added by Phase 0 with its reason recorded in
# decisions/phase0-mock.md and tests/fixtures/README.md ("Additions"). The reason above: without it
# every `wallet send --yes` against the mock 404s at the store step, i.e. AFTER the money moved --
# which is the AMBER row §4b names as "the mock asserts exactly one transfer and one relay_tx".
